question: What has TfL said about publishing section-level noise data?
norm_question: what has tfl said about publishing section level noise data

answer.text: TfL has released in-cab section-level noise measurements for the Central line in response to Freedom of Information requests (FOI-2986-2324 and FOI-1231-2425), states there is no requirement for annual whole-line measurements, and turned down the majority of Elly Baker AM's broader data requests citing constrained resources.

verified_claims.text: TfL has disclosed section-level in-cab noise measurements for the Central line between White City and Newbury Park in response to Freedom of Information requests FOI-2986-2324 and FOI-1231-2425.

citations.quote: levels and 1/3rd octaves in a Central line train cab recorded for the entire tunnel sections between White City and Newbury Park.
these measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab.

verified_claims.text: In FOI-3780-2324, TfL stated that there is no requirement to carry out annual noise measurements of an entire line, though it carries out measurements in known noise locations and on a bi-monthly period on the Central line.

citations.quote: There is no requirement to carry out annual noise measurements of an entire line. We do, however, carry out measurements on lines in known noise locations.
Readings are carried out on a bi-monthly period.

verified_claims.text: At Mayor's Question Time on 16 July 2026, Elly Baker AM reported that TfL's Government Relations team turned down the majority of her requests for data, stating that resources remain constrained.

citations.quote: just an email from TfL's Government Relations turning down the majority of the requests for data. It contained the reassuring phrase, "We are fully committed to tackling Tube noise, but – as you have said – resources remain constrained".
